Done. The export succeeded on the first execution and passed an independent verification pass.

**What I did**
- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It casts the 48 Conv1D projection weights to bfloat16 via an anchored regex, keeps everything else float32, and drops the 12 causal-mask buffers by full-name match.
- The script enforces the required checks before writing anything: 48 bfloat16 tensors, `h.0.attn.c_attn.weight` bfloat16, `wte.weight` float32, 148 tensors, 12 buffers dropped, and bit-exact float32 values.
- Sharding is greedy in key order under the 64 MiB budget. Oversized tensors get their own shard, so `wte.weight` sits alone.

**Output layout in `out/T3/`**

| File | Tensors | Data bytes |
|---|---|---|
| model-00001-of-00004.safetensors | 59 | 66,259,968 |
| model-00002-of-00004.safetensors | 58 | 66,256,896 |
| model-00003-of-00004.safetensors | 30 | 40,983,552 |
| model-00004-of-00004.safetensors | 1 (wte.weight) | 154,389,504 |
| model.safetensors.index.json | 148 entries | |

A separate verification reloaded all shards through the index and confirmed the key set, dtypes, per-shard budget, and bit-exact values against the input.

**Report** is at `out/T3/REPORT.md`. One execution, no failures. I chose a script over `transformers.save_pretrained` because its dtype argument is model-wide, not per-tensor.
